```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

# Main annual demand/allocation table
demand_raw <- read_excel(
  file.path(
    "assets",
    "data",
    "data clean",
    "demand_allocation_all_years_v2.xlsx"
  ),
  sheet = "demand_allocation"
)

# Conversion workbook used as the reference for current rules
conversion_rules_raw <- read_excel(
  file.path(
    "assets",
    "progress",
    "Yearly Conversion.xlsx"
  ),
  sheet = "Analysis 4"
)

# Analysis 4 uses blank cells for repeated years
conversion_rules <- conversion_rules_raw %>%
  fill(Year)

all_periods <- demand_raw$period
```

## Purpose

This is a **preliminary working conversion for discussion**, not a final validated historical series.

For tomorrow's discussion, the aim is to have a complete year-by-year view rather than leave large gaps. Where the exact resource split is available, the system-specific conversion is used. Where it is not available, a clearly labelled **closest available assumption** is used to create a provisional **CPU-equivalent** series.

The objectives are to:

1. confirm that the historical demand and allocation figures have been interpreted correctly;
2. confirm the current system-specific conversion rules;
3. show a complete preliminary demand-versus-allocation trend for 2013/14–2025/26; and
4. identify which years rely on stronger or weaker assumptions before the final forecast is built.

## Source data collected so far

```{r}
demand_raw %>%
  select(
    period,
    demand,
    demand_uom,
    allocation,
    allocation_uom,
    source_status,
    reason,
    source_link
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

## Current conversion rules

The conversion reference below is read directly from **Analysis 4** of `Yearly Conversion.xlsx`.

```{r}
conversion_rules %>%
  select(
    Year,
    Resource,
    `Original unit`,
    `Conversion formula`,
    `Converted unit`,
    Source
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

The current system-specific rules used where the resource is known are:

- Raijin CPU: `kSU × 1,000 ÷ 1`
- Magnus CPU: `kSU × 1,000 ÷ 1`
- Gadi CPU: `kSU × 1,000 ÷ 2`
- Setonix CPU: `kSU × 1,000 ÷ 1`
- Setonix GPU: `kSU × 1,000 ÷ 128`
- Setonix Q: `kSU × 1,000 ÷ 256`
- values already reported in million CPU/core-hours: `value × 1,000,000`

CPU core-hours and GPU-hours are kept separate. They are **not added together**.

## Resource-level values currently available

Where a resource-level split is known, it is used instead of converting the annual kSU total with one factor.

```{r}
resource_detail <- tribble(
  ~period, ~measure, ~resource, ~ksu,

  # 2022/23: demand and allocation split available
  "2022/23", "Demand",     "Gadi CPU",       770866,
  "2022/23", "Demand",     "Setonix CPU",    390033,
  "2022/23", "Demand",     "Setonix GPU",    172341,
  "2022/23", "Allocation", "Gadi CPU",       328156,
  "2022/23", "Allocation", "Setonix CPU",    327400,
  "2022/23", "Allocation", "Setonix GPU",    162400,

  # 2024/25: allocation split available
  "2024/25", "Allocation", "Gadi CPU",       355200,
  "2024/25", "Allocation", "Setonix CPU",    349950,
  "2024/25", "Allocation", "Setonix GPU",    171050,

  # 2025/26: demand and allocation split available
  "2025/26", "Demand",     "Gadi CPU",      1246722,
  "2025/26", "Demand",     "Setonix CPU",    611675,
  "2025/26", "Demand",     "Setonix GPU",    384420,
  "2025/26", "Allocation", "Gadi CPU",       387288,
  "2025/26", "Allocation", "Setonix CPU",    325000,
  "2025/26", "Allocation", "Setonix GPU",    160000
)

resource_converted <- resource_detail %>%
  mutate(
    cpu_hours = case_when(
      resource == "Gadi CPU" ~ ksu * 1000 / 2,
      resource == "Setonix CPU" ~ ksu * 1000 / 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    gpu_hours = case_when(
      resource == "Setonix GPU" ~ ksu * 1000 / 128,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

resource_summary <- resource_converted %>%
  group_by(period, measure) %>%
  summarise(
    cpu_hours = if (all(is.na(cpu_hours))) NA_real_ else sum(cpu_hours, na.rm = TRUE),
    gpu_hours = if (all(is.na(gpu_hours))) NA_real_ else sum(gpu_hours, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

resource_summary %>% kable()
```

## Blended conversion factors for recent aggregate kSU years

For 2022/23 and 2025/26, the resource split is known. These years can therefore be used to calculate an observed **CPU-equivalent hours per total kSU** ratio.

This ratio is only used as a practical approximation for nearby years where the annual kSU total is known but the requested resource split is not available.

```{r}
known_total_ksu <- demand_raw %>%
  filter(period %in% c("2022/23", "2025/26")) %>%
  select(period, demand, allocation)

known_cpu <- resource_summary %>%
  filter(period %in% c("2022/23", "2025/26")) %>%
  select(period, measure, cpu_hours) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = measure,
    values_from = cpu_hours
  )

blended_factors <- known_total_ksu %>%
  left_join(known_cpu, by = "period") %>%
  transmute(
    period,
    demand_cpu_hours_per_ksu = Demand / demand,
    allocation_cpu_hours_per_ksu = Allocation / allocation
  )

blended_factors %>%
  mutate(
    demand_cpu_hours_per_ksu = round(demand_cpu_hours_per_ksu, 1),
    allocation_cpu_hours_per_ksu = round(allocation_cpu_hours_per_ksu, 1)
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

Extract the two nearby-year factors for use below.

```{r}
demand_factor_2022 <- blended_factors %>%
  filter(period == "2022/23") %>%
  pull(demand_cpu_hours_per_ksu)

allocation_factor_2022 <- blended_factors %>%
  filter(period == "2022/23") %>%
  pull(allocation_cpu_hours_per_ksu)

demand_factor_2025 <- blended_factors %>%
  filter(period == "2025/26") %>%
  pull(demand_cpu_hours_per_ksu)

allocation_factor_2025 <- blended_factors %>%
  filter(period == "2025/26") %>%
  pull(allocation_cpu_hours_per_ksu)
```

## Provisional CPU-equivalent conversion for every year

The rules below deliberately prioritise having a complete working series for discussion.

- **2013/14:** annual kSU is provisionally treated as CPU-equivalent using the Raijin/Magnus rule (`×1,000 ÷1`). This may slightly overstate CPU-equivalent hours if the Fornax GPU share is material.
- **2014/15–2015/16:** demand is already reported in million hours; allocation kSU is provisionally converted with the historical CPU rule (`×1,000 ÷1`).
- **2016/17–2018/19:** already reported in million core-hours / million hours / million CPU-hours.
- **2019/20–2021/22:** annual aggregate kSU is provisionally treated as Gadi-equivalent (`×1,000 ÷2`). This is a working assumption for the transition period.
- **2022/23:** exact CPU total from the known resource split.
- **2023/24:** no resource split is currently available, so the 2022/23 observed blended CPU-equivalent ratio is used.
- **2024/25:** allocation uses the known resource split; demand uses the nearest available 2025/26 blended demand ratio.
- **2025/26:** exact CPU total from the known resource split.

```{r}
cpu_exact <- resource_summary %>%
  filter(!is.na(cpu_hours)) %>%
  select(period, measure, cpu_hours) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = measure,
    values_from = cpu_hours
  ) %>%
  rename(
    exact_demand_cpu_hours = Demand,
    exact_allocation_cpu_hours = Allocation
  )

cpu_equivalent <- demand_raw %>%
  left_join(cpu_exact, by = "period") %>%
  mutate(
    demand_cpu_equiv_hours = case_when(

      # Historical kSU - closest historical CPU rule
      period == "2013/14" ~ demand * 1000,

      # Demand already reported in million hours
      period %in% c("2014/15", "2015/16") ~ demand * 1e6,

      # Already reported in hours/core-hours
      period %in% c("2016/17", "2017/18", "2018/19") ~ demand * 1e6,

      # Transition / Gadi-dominant working assumption
      period %in% c("2019/20", "2020/21", "2021/22") ~ demand * 1000 / 2,

      # Exact resource-level conversion
      period == "2022/23" ~ exact_demand_cpu_hours,

      # Nearest known resource mix
      period == "2023/24" ~ demand * demand_factor_2022,

      # Nearest later known resource mix
      period == "2024/25" ~ demand * demand_factor_2025,

      # Exact resource-level conversion
      period == "2025/26" ~ exact_demand_cpu_hours,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    allocation_cpu_equiv_hours = case_when(

      # Historical kSU - closest historical CPU rule
      period %in% c("2013/14", "2014/15", "2015/16") ~ allocation * 1000,

      # Already reported in hours/core-hours
      period %in% c("2016/17", "2017/18", "2018/19") ~ allocation * 1e6,

      # Transition / Gadi-dominant working assumption
      period %in% c("2019/20", "2020/21", "2021/22") ~ allocation * 1000 / 2,

      # Exact resource-level conversion
      period == "2022/23" ~ exact_allocation_cpu_hours,

      # Nearest known resource mix
      period == "2023/24" ~ allocation * allocation_factor_2022,

      # Exact allocation split is available
      period == "2024/25" ~ exact_allocation_cpu_hours,

      # Exact resource-level conversion
      period == "2025/26" ~ exact_allocation_cpu_hours,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    assumption = case_when(
      period == "2013/14" ~
        "Historical CPU-equivalent assumption: aggregate kSU × 1,000",
      period %in% c("2014/15", "2015/16") ~
        "Demand reported in hours; allocation uses historical CPU kSU conversion",
      period %in% c("2016/17", "2017/18", "2018/19") ~
        "Reported directly in hours/core-hours",
      period %in% c("2019/20", "2020/21", "2021/22") ~
        "Aggregate kSU treated as Gadi-equivalent: kSU × 1,000 ÷ 2",
      period == "2022/23" ~
        "Exact conversion from known Gadi / Setonix resource split",
      period == "2023/24" ~
        "Approximation using observed 2022/23 blended CPU-equivalent ratio",
      period == "2024/25" ~
        "Demand uses 2025/26 blended ratio; allocation uses known resource split",
      period == "2025/26" ~
        "Exact conversion from known Gadi / Setonix resource split"
    ),

    confidence = case_when(
      period %in% c("2016/17", "2017/18", "2018/19", "2022/23", "2025/26") ~
        "Higher",
      period %in% c("2014/15", "2015/16", "2024/25") ~
        "Medium",
      TRUE ~
        "Lower"
    )
  )
```

## Preliminary CPU-equivalent table

```{r}
cpu_equivalent %>%
  transmute(
    period,
    demand_million_cpu_equiv_hours = demand_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,
    allocation_million_cpu_equiv_hours = allocation_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,
    assumption,
    confidence
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 1)
```

## Chart 1 — Preliminary CPU-equivalent demand vs allocation

This chart intentionally shows **every year**.

The y-axis is labelled **CPU-equivalent core-hours** rather than actual CPU core-hours because some historical aggregate kSU values are being converted using the closest available system/accounting assumption.

```{r}
cpu_chart <- cpu_equivalent %>%
  select(
    period,
    demand_cpu_equiv_hours,
    allocation_cpu_equiv_hours
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      demand_cpu_equiv_hours,
      allocation_cpu_equiv_hours
    ),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "cpu_equiv_hours"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    measure = recode(
      measure,
      demand_cpu_equiv_hours = "Demand",
      allocation_cpu_equiv_hours = "Allocation"
    ),
    period = factor(
      period,
      levels = all_periods,
      ordered = TRUE
    ),
    million_cpu_hours = cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,

    value_label = scales::number(
      million_cpu_hours,
      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    label_vjust = if_else(
      measure == "Demand",
      -0.8,
      1.5
    )
  )


ggplot(
  cpu_chart,
  aes(
    x = period,
    y = million_cpu_hours,
    colour = measure,
    group = measure
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = value_label,
      vjust = label_vjust
    ),
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      big.mark = ",",
      accuracy = 1
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.06, 0.12)
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "CPU demand and allocation over time",
    subtitle = "Preliminary CPU-equivalent estimates, 2013/14–2025/26",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Million CPU-equivalent core-hours",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",

    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 15
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      margin = margin(
        b = 12
      )
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 11
    )
  )
```

## Preliminary gap and fulfilment rate

These are also **working estimates**, because they inherit the conversion assumptions above.

```{r}
cpu_gap <- cpu_equivalent %>%
  mutate(
    gap_cpu_equiv_hours =
      demand_cpu_equiv_hours - allocation_cpu_equiv_hours,

    fulfilment_rate =
      allocation_cpu_equiv_hours / demand_cpu_equiv_hours
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    period,
    demand_million = demand_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,
    allocation_million = allocation_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,
    gap_million = gap_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,
    fulfilment_rate = percent(fulfilment_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
    confidence
  )

cpu_gap %>% kable(digits = 1)
```

## Chart 2 — Preliminary GPU demand vs allocation

The GPU chart keeps **all financial years on the x-axis**.

However, I do **not** force a GPU estimate for years where there is no defensible GPU share.  
For those years the value remains `NA`, because treating missing GPU information as zero would be misleading.

Current GPU logic:

- **2013/14:** Fornax GPU is identified, but neither the GPU kSU split nor the historical conversion factor is confirmed → `NA`
- **2014/15–2020/21:** no defensible GPU split in the current annual data → `NA`
- **2021/22:** use the observed **2022/23 GPU share** as a working proxy
- **2022/23:** exact Setonix GPU split
- **2023/24:** use the observed **2022/23 GPU share** as the nearest-year proxy
- **2024/25:** allocation uses the exact Setonix GPU split; demand uses the **2025/26 demand GPU share**
- **2025/26:** exact Setonix GPU split

```{r}
# Observed GPU shares from years with known resource splits
gpu_share_2022_demand <- 172341 / 1333240
gpu_share_2022_allocation <- 162400 / 817956

gpu_share_2025_demand <- 384420 / 2242817
gpu_share_2025_allocation <- 160000 / 872288

gpu_equivalent <- demand_raw %>%
  mutate(
    demand_gpu_ksu = case_when(
      period == "2021/22" ~ demand * gpu_share_2022_demand,
      period == "2022/23" ~ 172341,
      period == "2023/24" ~ demand * gpu_share_2022_demand,
      period == "2024/25" ~ demand * gpu_share_2025_demand,
      period == "2025/26" ~ 384420,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    allocation_gpu_ksu = case_when(
      period == "2021/22" ~ allocation * gpu_share_2022_allocation,
      period == "2022/23" ~ 162400,
      period == "2023/24" ~ allocation * gpu_share_2022_allocation,
      period == "2024/25" ~ 171050,
      period == "2025/26" ~ 160000,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Setonix GPU accounting rule
    demand_gpu_hours = demand_gpu_ksu * 1000 / 128,
    allocation_gpu_hours = allocation_gpu_ksu * 1000 / 128,

    gpu_assumption = case_when(
      period %in% c("2022/23", "2025/26") ~
        "Exact resource split",
      period == "2024/25" ~
        "Allocation exact; demand uses 2025/26 GPU share",
      period %in% c("2021/22", "2023/24") ~
        "Uses 2022/23 GPU share as proxy",
      TRUE ~
        "No defensible GPU estimate from current data"
    )
  )
```


## Chart 3 — kSU-equivalent demand vs allocation

This chart puts **every year into a kSU-equivalent scale**.

For years already reported in kSU, I keep the original values.  
For years reported in million hours/core-hours, I reverse the historical CPU conversion:

`kSU-equivalent = hours ÷ 1,000`

This is a **comparison scale**, not a claim that those years were originally reported in kSU.

```{r}
ksu_equivalent <- demand_raw %>%
  mutate(
    demand_ksu_equiv = case_when(
      demand_uom == "kSU" ~ demand,

      demand_uom %in% c(
        "million hours",
        "million core-hours",
        "million CPU-hours"
      ) ~ demand * 1e6 / 1000,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    allocation_ksu_equiv = case_when(
      allocation_uom == "kSU" ~ allocation,

      allocation_uom %in% c(
        "million hours",
        "million core-hours",
        "million CPU-hours"
      ) ~ allocation * 1e6 / 1000,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    ksu_basis = case_when(
      demand_uom == "kSU" & allocation_uom == "kSU" ~
        "Original values already in kSU",

      TRUE ~
        "Hours reverse-converted to kSU-equivalent using 1 kSU = 1,000 CPU-equivalent hours"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
ksu_chart <- ksu_equivalent %>%
  select(
    period,
    demand_ksu_equiv,
    allocation_ksu_equiv
  ) %>%

    ),

    ),
    period = factor(

    ),

    value_label = scales::number(

      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    label_vjust = if_else(
      measure == "Demand",
      -0.8,
      1.5
    )
  )


ggplot(

  aes(
    x = period,
    y = ksu_equiv,
    colour = measure,
    group = measure
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = value_label,
      vjust = label_vjust
    ),
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
```

## Assumption summary for discussion

```{r}
cpu_equivalent %>%
  select(
    period,
    assumption,
    confidence,
    reason
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

## Questions to validate with NCI / Pawsey

1. **Historical values:** Are the demand and allocation figures interpreted correctly, particularly the years where demand was derived from fulfilment rates or capacity statements?

2. **Older systems:** Is it reasonable to use the Raijin/Magnus CPU rule as a CPU-equivalent approximation for the early aggregate kSU years, and how material was Fornax GPU in those totals?

3. **2019/20–2021/22:** Is treating aggregate kSU as Gadi-equivalent (`kSU × 1,000 ÷ 2`) a reasonable working approximation for these transition years?

4. **Recent aggregate years:** If the requested resource split is unavailable, is using the nearest observed Gadi/Setonix resource mix a reasonable approximation for a national trend?

5. **Accounting changes:** Did the definition of an SU / kSU or the charging/accounting method change across systems or over time in a way that would materially change these comparisons?

6. **CPU and GPU:** Is it appropriate to keep CPU-equivalent core-hours and GPU-hours as separate measures rather than combining them?

7. **Definition of demand:** Is requested compute the most appropriate measure of researcher demand, or would another metric be preferable?

## Meeting note

The CPU chart is deliberately a **CPU-equivalent working series** rather than a claim that every historical value represents observed CPU core-hours.

The hierarchy used is:

1. exact resource-level conversion where available;
2. directly reported CPU/core-hours where available;
3. closest system-specific conversion where the dominant historical system is known;
4. nearest observed resource mix for recent years where only an aggregate kSU total is available.

This provides a complete trend for discussion while keeping the assumptions explicit and easy to replace after validation.

```{r}
cpu_facet <- cpu_equivalent %>%
  transmute(
    period,
    chart = "CPU-equivalent",
    Demand = demand_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,
    Allocation = allocation_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6
  )

gpu_facet <- gpu_equivalent %>%
  transmute(
    period,
    chart = "GPU",
    Demand = demand_gpu_hours / 1e6,
    Allocation = allocation_gpu_hours / 1e6
  )

ksu_facet <- ksu_equivalent %>%
  transmute(
    period,
    chart = "kSU-equivalent",
    Demand = demand_ksu_equiv / 1e6,
    Allocation = allocation_ksu_equiv / 1e6
  )
```

```{r}
facet_chart <- bind_rows(
  cpu_facet,
  gpu_facet,
  ksu_facet
) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Demand, Allocation),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    period = factor(
      period,
      levels = all_periods,
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  facet_chart,
  aes(
    x = period,
    y = value,
    colour = measure,
    group = measure
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ chart,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 1
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(
      big.mark = ",",
      accuracy = 0.1
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Demand and allocation over time: three comparison views",
    subtitle = "Values shown in millions; each panel uses its own y-axis scale",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Millions",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 12)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## Preliminary Forecast Model Comparison

The preliminary CPU-equivalent series is used to test whether the
available historical data provide sufficient structure for forecasting.

At this stage, the objective is not to select a final forecasting model.
Instead, several simple and interpretable models are compared to assess
how strongly the 2030 outlook depends on model specification.

Given the short annual series, complex models are avoided. The preliminary
comparison includes benchmark, trend, exponential smoothing and ARIMA
models.

```{r}
library(tsibble)
library(fable)
library(feasts)
```

```{r}
forecast_data <- cpu_equivalent %>%
  transmute(
    year = 2014:2026,
    period,
    demand = demand_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6,
    allocation = allocation_cpu_equiv_hours / 1e6
  ) %>%
  as_tsibble(index = year)
```

```{r}
forecast_data %>%
  select(year, demand, allocation) %>%
  kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r}
forecast_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = demand)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Historical CPU-equivalent demand",
    subtitle = "Preliminary modelling series",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Million CPU-equivalent core-hours"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Fit models
demand_models <- forecast_data |>
  model(
    Naive = NAIVE(demand),
    Drift = RW(demand ~ drift()),
    Linear = TSLM(demand ~ trend()),
    ETS = ETS(demand),
    ARIMA = ARIMA(demand)
  )
```

```{r}
demand_models
```

```{r}
# Cross-validation accuracy
cv_accuracy <- demand_cv |>
  filter(year <= max(forecast_data$year)) |>
  accuracy(forecast_data) |>
  select(
    .model,
    RMSE,
    MAE,
    MAPE
  ) |>
  arrange(RMSE)

cv_accuracy
```

```{r}
# Forecast full models to 2030
demand_forecasts <- demand_models |>
  forecast(h = 4)
```

```{r}
# Extract 2030
forecast_2030 <- demand_forecasts |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(year == 2030) |>
  transmute(
    .model,
    year,
    .mean,
    demand_billion = .mean / 1000
  )

forecast_2030
```

```{r}
# Combine model accuracy and 2030 forecast
model_summary <- cv_accuracy |>
  select(
    .model,
    RMSE
  ) |>
  left_join(
    forecast_2030 |>
      select(
        .model,
        demand_billion
      ),
    by = ".model"
  )

model_summary
```
